  "markdown_report": "**Recommendation:** retain the fixed 0.5 terminal/reconstruction BERT4Rec objective and strengthen the bounded sampled-versus-full-catalog audit with an exact sampling reference. At 40% progress, this is a feasible measurement step; it does not replace the starting hypothesis’s controlled training comparison.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, sampler and serialized-serving checks pass across all four categories within tested coverage. They establish neither recommendation quality nor external-label invariance. Second, recent deletion lowers mean target scores everywhere, but diagnostic hit@10 intervals include zero. Greater recency emphasis remains unverified. Third, equal branch coefficients do not imply equal optimization influence. Simultaneous weighted losses and randomly alternating objectives can differ under Adam despite matching expected gradients.

**Insights from related work.** First, BERT4Rec already includes terminal examples and sequence-normalized reconstruction [1]; allocation changes are controlled ablations. Second, sampled metrics can reverse aggregate model comparisons [2], although expected sampled hits remain monotone in full rank for a fixed eligible catalog size. Third, negative-sampling effects vary across popularity groups [3]; descriptive frequency strata cannot establish exposure mechanisms.

These insights organize into supervision allocation, candidate competition, and measurement reliability:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Allocation | Fixed mixture with sequence means | Sustained terminal benefit versus T/R controls |
| Competition | Random-negative margins | Eligible-catalog boundary and sampling distortion |
| Reliability | Serving parity passes | Numerical reproducibility and diagnostic predictive value |

Three atomic proposals follow; scores denote originality/potential/difficulty, with higher difficulty meaning harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Paired catalog-boundary audit** [2,3] | 3/6/4 | Originality: integrates paired strata; established mathematics. Potential: explains candidate effects; remains in-sample. Difficulty: frozen scoring is simple; deterministic streaming requires care. |
| Corruption-preserving one-target reconstruction control [1] | 3/6/4 | Originality: isolates supervision variance; standard estimator. Potential: clarifies reduction effects; terminal context remains unmatched. Difficulty: reuses masks; needs sampler instrumentation. |
| Transactional branch-omission audit [4,5] | 5/6/8 | Originality: optimizer-aware adaptation; established influence methods. Potential: measures local transfer; lasting gains unproven. Difficulty: reuses losses; exact rollback is demanding. |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze one trained model/category. Preselect up to 32 training users/category and one eligible endpoint/user independently of scores. Reuse canonical catalog scores for both exhaustive ranking and 99 unique uniformly sampled competitors. Report ranks, paired hit disagreement, target-minus-tenth-competitor margins, and tenth–eleventh competitor gaps, with frozen training-frequency/history-length strata.

For eligible size N including the target and full rank r, X~Hypergeometric(N−1,r−1,99); expected sampled hit is P(X≤9), and expected sampled rank is 1+99(r−1)/(N−1). Average probabilities per user. Observed disagreement is sampling behavior, not automatically a model defect.

Pin chunk shapes, precision and total tie order; stream eligible top-11 and count ranks using scores from identical passes [6–8]. Predeclare compute caps and report partial coverage. Preserve host macro validation HR@10, four routes, seeds, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. No gain or shortcut-removal claim follows. References [1–8] are linked below.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add a preregistered, bounded paired sampled/full-catalog boundary audit with an exact without-replacement sampling reference to the fixed simultaneous 0.5 terminal/reconstruction BERT4Rec experiment, using exactly one frozen trained model per category.",
    "motivation": "Supplied diagnostics support serving consistency within tested coverage and conditional history sensitivity, but provide neither host validation gains nor full-catalog ranking evidence. Identical-query candidate comparisons can reveal competition concealed by random-negative margins and quantify the sampling behavior expected from each full rank and eligible catalog size. This is relevant because native recommendations use the eligible full catalog while selection uses pinned sampled macro validation HR@10. The audit is a measurement contribution, not a demonstrated training improvement or a replacement for terminal/reconstruction controls.",
    "implementation_notes": "Keep the corrected BERT4Rec architecture and preregistered objective unchanged. Define T as the mean of terminal-target sequence losses and R as the mean across sequences of each sequence's mean supervised reconstruction loss. Compute L=0.5*T+0.5*R before one optimizer update. Prefer paired terminal and reconstruction views of the same sampled windows, with unchanged base batch size; record both views' compute. This simultaneous objective must not silently become random objective selection or half-batch allocation: these change exposure or gradient variance and can change Adam updates. Equal coefficients do not equalize gradients, targets or GPU cost. Record branch sequence counts, target counts, loss denominators, tokens, forward/backward passes and GPU-seconds. This proposal adds measurement, without adaptive weighting, repairs or another predictor.

Specify the reconstruction sampler from the supplied corrected baseline, including mask rate, eligible positions, endpoint participation, all-MASK replacement policy, empty-mask handling, negative sampling, window distribution and loss type. Do not substitute a paper's sampler for the actual host implementation. Terminal construction masks the sampled endpoint and excludes later interactions; reconstruction retains its declared bidirectional visible context. Repeated historical occurrences of the terminal ID remain legitimate context and should be counted rather than removed. The audit's unseen-target restriction creates a narrower population than unrestricted training and must be reported.

The starting training hypothesis remains unresolved without T-only, R-only and simultaneous-mixture controls. Treat these as separately budgeted future trials, never as extra deployed predictors or promised affordable runs. Each trial independently trains one model/category from identical seed-42 initialization, with matched users/endpoints/windows, separate sampling/corruption RNG streams, reuse of each objective's corruption across applicable arms, identical optimizer settings and update counts. Keep base sequence exposure comparable and report unavoidable target/context/compute differences. A fixed-update comparison and an identical predeclared validation/checkpoint cadence distinguish optimization duration from checkpoint selection. If category checkpoints are selected separately, freeze that policy identically across arms and compare the resulting four-category collections through host macro HR@10; do not describe separate category selection as a jointly selected macro checkpoint. A small non-updating gradient audit may measure branch norms, weighted norms and cosine on fixed paired minibatches with controlled dropout and restored RNG. Negative cosine alone establishes neither downstream harm nor a need for reweighting [5].

Before the catalog audit, freeze a protocol manifest: at most 32 users/category, minimum prefix length four, endpoint eligibility, candidate seed 42, deterministic identity ordering, exact frequency/history bins, user-selection procedure, software/hardware and numerical settings, and a diagnostic compute cap within the remaining shared budget. Remaining runtime is unspecified, so do not promise additional training arms. A concrete default is target-frequency bins 1–4, 5–16, 17–64 and >=65 training occurrences, and visible-history bins 4–7, 8–15 and >=16. Count frequencies exclusively from permitted training histories; state that these are descriptive corpus statistics, not temporally causal exposure estimates.

Enumerate users in a stable order, use a dedicated generator to permute them without inspecting scores, and select up to 32 eligible users. For each, sample uniformly one public training endpoint with at least four preceding interactions and a real target absent from the complete preceding prefix. Later interactions never determine candidate eligibility. Record scanned/selected users, endpoint counts and exclusions. The selected users are not independent held-out validation users. Do not inspect hidden labels or other trials.

Build the serving query from at most maxlen-1 preceding items, left pad, append the reserved MASK, and read the actual final nonpadding position, never count-1. Do not include the endpoint target as visible input. Keep absolute positions identical across candidate-set comparisons. Use model.eval() and torch.inference_mode(); freeze the query feature once. Score through the actual trained scoring head, including any transformation or item bias, using view.log2feats and view.predict_score. Retain view.item_emb and view.model as the actual trained network. Encoder attention remains bidirectional with padding keys masked.

The eligible universe contains the target plus every real catalog item absent from the complete preceding prefix, including interactions truncated from the encoder input. PAD and MASK never compete. Sample 99 unique competitors uniformly without replacement using a dedicated per-example candidate generator. Persist sampled IDs and the protocol manifest. Fewer than 99 eligible competitors yields an explicitly unavailable sampled comparison. Unobserved items are unlabeled competitors, not verified dislikes. Prefix exclusions can differ from other evaluation conventions; describe this audit's universe without claiming it reproduces the host evaluator.

Use a fixed user batch size, ascending real-item IDs, pinned catalog chunk size, scoring dtype, TF32/autocast policy, deterministic settings, library versions and hardware. Keep chunk boundaries and shapes identical in repeated passes. Check raw real-item scores with torch.isfinite before applying exclusions; any NaN/Inf invalidates the affected query rather than being repaired. Filter excluded IDs before selection so sentinel values cannot enter short lists. Obtain the target score from its canonical catalog chunk and collect sampled competitors' scores during that same traversal. Reuse these canonical scores for sampled ranks and margins rather than rescoring candidates separately.

Order all diagnostic candidates by descending computed score, then ascending item ID. Sort IDs ascending before stable descending argsort; ordinary topk does not guarantee tie membership [7]. Stream the top 11 eligible competitors by merging retained entries with each chunk's eligible top 11 under the same total order. Target rank requires competitors outside the top 11: either cache all eligible scores if memory permits, or make a second identical catalog pass and count competitors preceding the canonical target. In a two-pass implementation, require exact equality of repeated target, sampled and retained boundary scores; record this as a limited repeatability check, not proof that every score is identical. If repeatability fails, use cached canonical scores or mark exhaustive rank unavailable. Pinning shapes reduces, but does not eliminate, numerical variability [8]. 'Exact rank' means exhaustive ordering of the computed scores, not platform-independent real-arithmetic ranking. Never introduce epsilon ties.

Let N be the eligible universe size including the target, and let r be its one-based exhaustive rank under that total order. For 99 uniformly sampled unique competitors, X, the number ahead, follows Hypergeometric(N-1,r-1,99). Expected sampled rank is 1+99*(r-1)/(N-1). Expected sampled hit@10 is P(X<=9), computed with scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9,N-1,r-1,99), with explicit N>=100 and 1<=r<=N checks. Impossible combinations contribute zero. Average these per-user probabilities rather than substituting mean rank or mean catalog size. At fixed N the expected hit is monotone in r; aggregate model-comparison reversal requires different rank distributions and is not established by one-model distortion. At fixed r, larger N generally makes sampling easier by reducing the fraction of ahead competitors. Treat these as mathematical references, not empirical model gains.

Compute observed sampled/full target ranks, hit@10 and both directions of paired disagreement, plus expected sampled hit and expected sampled rank. With identical canonical scores and nested competitors, full rank cannot improve over sampled rank; a full-catalog hit must also be a sampled hit. Violations indicate an implementation inconsistency. Report observed-minus-expected sampled hits descriptively; one sampled set per query is noisy and does not support a sampling-calibration claim. Full-catalog HR@10 and expected sampled HR@10 answer different questions.

Define each candidate-set target margin as target score minus its tenth-highest eligible competitor score. Define its competitor boundary gap as tenth-highest minus eleventh-highest competitor score. These are competitor-only boundaries: for a target already within top ten, they are not necessarily the tenth/eleventh gap of the complete list including the target. The margin's sign alone does not determine a tie-resolved hit when it equals zero; use the total-order rank. Insufficient competitor counts produce unavailable values. Save raw paired outcomes, counts and frozen descriptive strata; avoid strong conclusions for small cells. If budgeted, use 500 user-level bootstrap replicates with a separate seed-42 generator. Such intervals describe sampled-user uncertainty conditional on the fitted model, selected population and fixed sampled candidates, not training-seed or full candidate-sampling uncertainty.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions with actual dataset identity, completion counts, definitions, exclusions, nonfinite observations, numerical/repeatability settings and elapsed time. Preserve the B x L loader contract, family-specific sample_batch and all ModelView interfaces. Gate serving-sensitive interpretation on sampler and serialized-serving parity across short, full-length, truncated and batched inputs. Preserve existing measured probes and explicit availability reporting; run probes independently so an unrelated failure does not erase completed measurements. The interpreter must distinguish measured observations, mathematical references and hypotheses.

Restore each module's individual training flag and all touched RNG states in finally blocks. Use dedicated diagnostic generators, avoid advancing the training iterator and perform no optimizer step. Set a concrete cap in the protocol manifest before execution, synchronize CUDA for timing, and check the cap between chunks/examples. Record cap overshoot, completed coverage and the stopping reason. If completion depends on variable catalog cost, partial outcomes are descriptive and must not be represented as the full preregistered sample. Aggregate category means with equal weights only when all four categories complete the declared protocol; never substitute a partial macro. Diagnostic macro summaries must be labeled separately from host macro validation HR@10.

Do not adapt training, bins, user selection or checkpoint choice using the audit outcomes within the same experiment. The audit can expose score dependence or popularity-associated heterogeneity but cannot establish shortcut learning, latent intent, exposure mechanisms or removal of bias. Training-prefix selection can favor memorized/easy examples; report that limitation. Repeatedly selecting ideas through the same host validation set can also create selection optimism; log all attempted configurations and do not claim significance from selected aggregate gains.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; exactly 200 batches per epoch; single-GPU execution; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Export exactly one independently trained checkpoint/category through the matching predictor writer; no checkpoint averaging, score fusion or separately fitted popularity/transition component. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five designated real training users/category independently of this audit's user sample. Use only permitted public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, reviews, product attributes and simulator traits remain unobserved. Select solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10 with its pinned candidates and seeds. Leave held-out evaluation to the host. No validation or full-catalog improvement is claimed.",
    "pseudocode": "preregister objective, protocol manifest, bins, user/candidate seeds and compute cap
# All training and audit computation consumes the shared search budget.
for category in the four required routes:
    initialize the supplied corrected BERT4Rec with training seed 42
    for each authorized epoch (at most 200):
        for update in range(200):
            windows = supplied_window_sampler(base_batch_size)
            terminal_view = mask_endpoint_without_later_context(windows)
            reconstruction_view = unchanged_declared_reconstruction_sampler(windows)
            T = mean(per_sequence_terminal_losses(terminal_view))
            R = mean(per_sequence_mean_masked_losses(reconstruction_view))
            update_one_model_once(0.5*T + 0.5*R)
            record sequences, targets, denominators, passes and compute
    export one selected category checkpoint and matching predictor
    require sampler and serialized-serving parity before sensitive interpretation
    snapshot individual module modes and touched random states
    try:
        model.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            select up to 32 training users/endpoints independently of scores
            for user, endpoint in selected examples:
                prefix, target = public_training_prefix(user, endpoint)
                competitors = real_items - set(prefix) - {target}
                if target is invalid or len(competitors) < 99:
                    record unavailable example; continue
                sampled_ids = uniform_sample_99_without_replacement(competitors)
                query = left_pad(prefix[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK])
                feature = log2feats(query)[actual_final_nonpadding_position]
                # Pinned ascending catalog chunks; use actual trained scoring head.
                for chunk in canonical_catalog_chunks:
                    enforce_declared_compute_cap_and_record_partial_status()
                    raw_scores = predict_score(feature, chunk)
                    require all real-item scores finite before exclusions
                    retain canonical target/sample scores
                    filter excluded IDs before selection
                    merge eligible competitor top11 with stable total ordering
                    optionally cache eligible scores for exhaustive rank
                if scores were not cached:
                    repeat identical chunks/shapes/settings to count ahead competitors
                    check repeated canonical scores; mark rank unavailable on mismatch
                full_rank = 1 + count_competitors_before_target_by_score_then_ID()
                sampled_rank = 1 + count_sampled_before_target_using_canonical_scores()
                require sampled_rank <= full_rank
                require not(full_rank <= 10 and sampled_rank > 10)
                N = len(competitors) + 1
                expected_hit = hypergeom.cdf(9, N-1, full_rank-1, 99)
                expected_rank = 1 + 99*(full_rank-1)/(N-1)
                record observed ranks/hits, expected values and paired disagreements
                record target-minus-tenth-competitor margins and competitor gaps
                record frozen frequency/history strata and raw outcomes
            return metrics, metric_definitions, counts, status and elapsed time
    finally:
        restore each module mode and touched random states
aggregate equal-weight category summaries only after all four complete
# Keep audit summaries distinct from host validation.
# Do not adapt objectives or checkpoints using audit users.
select using unchanged host macro validation HR@10
# T-only/R-only controls require separately budgeted independent trials;
# each trial still exports exactly one independently trained model/category.",
    "originality": {
      "score": 3,
      "positive": "Integrates canonical-score candidate comparisons, explicit catalog boundaries, frequency strata and an exact sampling reference into the constrained BERT4Rec workflow.",
      "negative": "Exhaustive ranking, hypergeometric sampling probabilities and popularity stratification are established; no new learning objective or statistical estimator is introduced."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 6,
      "positive": "Can distinguish expected candidate-sampling effects from implementation inconsistencies and guide a focused, separately validated single-model experiment.",
      "negative": "Training-prefix findings may reflect memorization and need not predict validation gains; the audit alone does not resolve the terminal/reconstruction hypothesis."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "Reuses frozen encoder features, the trained scoring head and standard hypergeometric routines without optimizer rollback or architecture changes.",
      "negative": "Canonical-score reuse, stable streaming ties, two-pass repeatability, complete-prefix eligibility and reliable partial-result reporting require more care than basic chunked scoring."
    }
  },
  "related_work": [
    {
      "title": "[1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690",
      "contributions": [
        "Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item inference.",
        "Includes terminal-only training examples and sequence-normalized masked-target losses, supporting careful allocation controls."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish the best terminal/reconstruction allocation for the supplied corrected host implementation.",
        "Its implementation must not be assumed identical to the host sampler.",
        "Provides no evidence of gains from this proposed audit."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[2] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation",
      "link": "https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/",
      "contributions": [
        "Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield inconsistent aggregate model comparisons, including in expectation.",
        "Motivates distinguishing sampled-candidate performance from full-catalog competition."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.",
        "Does not determine candidate-set effects in these four datasets.",
        "One model's sampled/full disagreement does not demonstrate reversal between models."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[3] Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276",
      "contributions": [
        "Reports dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-group tradeoffs under different negative-sampling choices.",
        "Motivates descriptive training-frequency strata alongside aggregate outcomes."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish that popularity-based sampling improves the corrected BERT4Rec here.",
        "Frequency strata cannot establish exposure mechanisms, shortcut learning or user preferences."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[4] LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04333",
      "contributions": [
        "Uses optimizer-aware gradient information for targeted influence estimation.",
        "Provides methodological inspiration for the alternative branch-transfer audit."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Studies a different learning setting and supplies no BERT4Rec validation evidence.",
        "Local influence estimates do not establish sustained ranking improvement."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[5] Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782",
      "contributions": [
        "Analyzes conflicting task gradients and proposes a gradient-projection method.",
        "Provides context for reporting branch gradient norms and cosine similarity."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Negative gradient cosine alone does not establish harmful terminal/reconstruction interaction.",
        "The proposed audit does not apply gradient surgery or infer that it would improve this benchmark."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[6] PyTorch torch.isfinite",
      "link": "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.isfinite.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Defines elementwise checks for finite scores before exclusions and ranking."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Finite scores do not establish correct candidate eligibility, numerical repeatability or recommendation quality."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[7] PyTorch torch.argsort and torch.topk",
      "link": "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.argsort.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Stable argsort supports a score-then-item-ID total order when IDs are initially ascending.",
        "The companion topk documentation states that tied indices are not guaranteed stable: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Stable ordering resolves exact computed-score ties but cannot prevent rounding from changing near-tie scores."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "[8] PyTorch Numerical Accuracy",
      "link": "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Explains floating-point differences between mathematically equivalent batched and sliced computations.",
        "Supports pinning shapes and precision settings and reusing canonical catalog scores."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Pinned settings do not guarantee bitwise reproducibility across hardware, library versions or execution paths.",
        "Exhaustive computed-score ranks are not platform-independent real-arithmetic ranks."
      ]
    }
  ]
